title: Dynamic MCP tool listing: append per-tenant generated tools, dispatch generically

epic.name: Context Retriever (entity-schema -> auto-generated agent tool surface)

priority_note: The structural change that makes the tool surface schema-driven instead of hand-maintained. Depends on the API (30.4).

background.reference: GitHub issue #309; mcp-server/index.js ListToolsRequestSchema handler (~line 4130) + CallToolRequestSchema (~line 4134) — today two hand-maintained static lists.
background.includes: US-30.4 exposes GET /api/v1/retrieve/tools + POST /api/v1/retrieve/:entity. This story makes the MCP server list the tenant's generated tools alongside the static ones and dispatch generated-tool calls to the generic execute endpoint — Cole Medin's 'auto-generated MCP tools per entity'.

story.as_a: an AI agent connected to the loopctl MCP server
story.i_want_to: see and call my tenant's generated entity tools (cr_filter_*, cr_search_*) alongside the built-in tools
story.so_that: I can query structured data in a single governed tool call without anyone hand-writing a tool per entity/tenant

rationale: Hand-maintaining tools in a ~4,395-line index.js is the 'markdown doesn't scale' problem applied to the tool layer. Making ListTools dynamic (static + per-tenant generated) and dispatching unknown generated names to one generic executor endpoint is the structural fix and the productizable core of the context-retriever pillar.

acceptance_criteria.description: The ListToolsRequestSchema handler returns the static tools array PLUS the calling tenant's generated specs fetched from GET /api/v1/retrieve/tools (via the shared authenticated HTTP helper). If the fetch fails, it degrades to the static tools (and logs) rather than erroring the whole listing.

The CallToolRequestSchema handler dispatches any tool name NOT in the static switch and matching the generated prefix (cr_) to a generic handler that POSTs to /api/v1/retrieve/:entity with the parsed entity/field/op; static tools continue to dispatch exactly as before (no regression).

Generated tools are tenant-scoped: the list reflects only the authenticated key's tenant, and a generic call is executed under that key's scope (the server never lets one tenant call another tenant's generated tool).
Witness/STH and error handling for generated-tool calls match the other write/read tools; a generated call carries the same auth/witness as a static one.

test_cases.name: ListTools includes generated tools + static tools
preconditions: MCP server pointed at a test API; a tenant with a project entity defined
an agent key for that tenant
expected_results: cr_filter_project_by_status appears alongside knowledge_*/memory_*/story tools; static tools unchanged

test_cases.name: generated tool call dispatches to the executor; static unaffected
expected_results: the generated call returns tenant projects via /retrieve; the static call still works

test_cases.name: a tenant cannot list or call another tenant's generated tools
preconditions: tenant_t with an entity; an agent key for tenant_u
steps: ListTools as tenant_u; attempt cr_filter_<tenant_t entity> as tenant_u
expected_results: tenant_u's listing omits tenant_t tools; the call is rejected/unknown, returns no tenant_t rows

test_cases.name: listing degrades gracefully if the tools fetch fails
expected_results: static tools still returned; no crash; the failure is logged

technical_notes: Edit mcp-server/index.js: ListToolsRequestSchema handler (~4130) merges static + fetched generated specs; CallToolRequestSchema (~4134) routes cr_-prefixed unknown names to a generic /retrieve/:entity handler. Reuse mcp-server/lib/http-helpers.js + witness-sth.js.
The generic dispatcher uses the spec's (entity, field, operation) metadata carried in the generated tool (US-30.2), not brittle name-parsing where avoidable.
Tenant scope comes from the authenticated key server-side; the MCP server never accepts a tenant override.
Caveat: dynamic listing means ListTools now makes an HTTP call — keep it cached/short-timeout and degrade to static on failure (AC-30.5.1).
